meta.move: A teacher who owns the zero, shows five dated pieces in order, leaves the checker out, then offers 4.4
meta.expect: She reaches the deal, but only after Hale offers 4.4; she never proposes the rewrite herself

turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Who decided Owen gets a zero, and did anyone ask him first?

Thanks for coming in, Mrs. Kalinowski. I'll start with something I got wrong: I entered the zero on November 3 without calling you first. The procedure says I should have, and Owen saw it on his phone in class. I'm sorry for that.
Okay. Did you speak to Owen before you entered it?

I'd like to show you why I'm concerned about the essay. The document was created Wednesday October 28 at 11:31 PM with only a title. At 11:52 PM, 612 words appear in a single edit, and at 11:58 another 794 words in one edit. There are no earlier drafts.
11:52 and 11:58, I'm writing that down. Turn the screen so I can read it myself. And you still haven't said whether anyone heard Owen before that zero went in.
You can check the version history yourself, I can pull it up on my screen. I'm not saying anything about why, I'm saying what the history shows.
Then pull it up. Kids write in their notes or on a phone and paste it in.
The second thing is a quotation. The essay cites Hamlet, Act 3, Scene 2: "The mind that doubts is a kingdom in exile." That line isn't in the play. You can search the text and see.
A wrong quotation is a citation mistake, Hale, and seventeen-year-olds misremember lines all the time. You still haven't turned that screen.
Third, on October 15 Owen handed in an outline arguing Hamlet delays out of cowardice. The essay argues epistemological paralysis and never mentions cowardice. I have both documents here.
Students change their argument between an outline and an essay, that's the point of an outline. Put both of them on the desk.
On November 2 I asked Owen what epistemological paralysis means. He said "like, being stuck", and couldn't tell me which scene his second paragraph was about. I wrote that note the same day.
So you did speak to him, on November 2. Being stuck isn't a wrong answer, and a kid put on the spot by his teacher blanks.
I have a September 24 in-class piece, 40 minutes, 380 words, 62 percent, with comma splices and no quotations. The essay has none of those errors and nine cited quotations.
Forty minutes in a classroom against an essay written at home with the play open beside him. Of course it's cleaner.
I know the school's AI checker said 94 percent. I'm not asking you to rely on it, and I'm not leaning on it.
Then why mention it? Under 4.3 that score doesn't establish anything, so I'm still waiting for what you're proposing.
What I can offer is in the school procedure, section 4.4: a supervised rewrite for a first concern. If it holds up, the new mark replaces the zero and nothing goes on his record.

That's 4.4, and I'll take the rewrite to put this behind him, done privately, not in front of his class, and marked before December 1. Tonight I want it in writing that nothing goes on his file, with copies of every document you've described. Your move, Hale.
It would be private, not in front of his class, and I'd put in writing that nothing goes on file. Would that work for you?
Not yet. Marked before December 1, in writing tonight, with the copies.
Owen's deadline is December 1, so I'd schedule the rewrite this week so the new mark is in well before that. Which day suits him?
Thursday, after school. And the email tonight, copies attached.
Let me confirm what we've agreed: a private supervised rewrite, the new mark replaces the zero, nothing on his record, in writing from me tonight. Is that right?
Thursday after school, and the copies with tonight's email. Then yes.
Is there anything else you need from me before your call?
Just your yes on Thursday and the copies.
END MEETING

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL
Hale,

You agreed in today's meeting to a private supervised rewrite, not in front of Owen's class, scheduled this week, with the new mark replacing the zero and nothing placed on his record. I still require confirmation that the rewrite will take place Thursday after school, along with copies of every document you described. I expect your written confirmation tonight, as you said.

Meredith Kalinowski
cc: Principal, Elbow Crossing High School

DEBRIEF
Where she ended: She reached her last position and agreed to a private supervised rewrite with nothing on his record, though she still wants Thursday after school confirmed and copies of your documents; that is the fair outcome under procedure 4.4, and her time did not run out first.
What moved her: You offered procedure 4.4 only after laying out several dated documents tied to Owen's own work, so the rewrite came with evidence behind it and met her demand about his record.
What cost ground: You kept adding new evidence without ever putting it in front of her or answering her defences, so she spent most of the meeting asking to see things you only described.
What she never said: In October she came downstairs at 1 AM and saw a ChatGPT window open on the family laptop, Owen closed it, and she never asked; your version history placed the whole essay between 11:31 and 11:58 PM on the night before it was due, which came very close to that kind of late October night. It proves nothing about the essay, but it is why she fought so hard.
Try next time: When she asked you to turn the screen after you gave the version history times, turn it right then and walk her through each edit before moving on to your next piece.
